texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a traveler of {FACTION}, stopped {A_nameDef} by the well and said a name {A_nameDef} hasn't used in years. {X_nameDef} remembers the face from the wanted posters, from when {A_nameDef} was {TALE}, and remembers the reward on it.\n\n{X_nameDef} would forget all about it for {COUNT} silver.

[lowtech] A traveler of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, kept staring at {A_nameDef} all morning, and finally took {A_objective} aside. There used to be a price on {A_nameDef}'s head, back when {A_pronoun} was {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} still remembers the drawing on the notice.\n\nFor {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will forget it.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} spent a long time looking at {A_nameDef} across the yard before coming over. {X_nameDef} has seen that face on a bounty list, from when {A_nameDef} was {TALE}, and thinks keeping it off the comms is worth {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Pay {X_objective} {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} pockets the silver, nods to {A_nameDef} and leaves before supper.

li.label: Call the bluff (they may talk)
li.outcome: The colony tells {X_nameDef} to say whatever {X_pronoun} likes. {X_nameDef} shrugs and leaves without another word, and that seems to be the end of it.
li.riskOutcome: The colony tells {X_nameDef} to say whatever {X_pronoun} likes, and {X_pronoun} does. Within days {FACTION} have heard all about what {A_nameDef} used to be.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} talk to {X_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} takes {X_nameDef} for a long walk around the fields. Whatever is said out there, {X_nameDef} comes back pale and leaves without asking for anything.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} talk behind the storehouse, and it goes badly. {X_nameDef} leaves in a hurry, promising that {FACTION} will hear about it.

remembered.li: [quiet] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} knows what {A_nameDef} used to be, and has kept quiet so far.
[talked] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} told {X_possessive} people what {A_nameDef} used to be.

texts.li: A rider of {FACTION} brought a letter for {A_nameDef}, sealed with an old unit badge. It's from {X_nameDef}, who commanded {A_objective} years ago and now leads {FACTION}'s fighters against {ENEMY}. The campaign is short of supplies, and {X_nameDef} asks, as a favor to an old comrade, for {TALE}.\n\nIf it goes well, {X_nameDef} writes, the colony will get a share of the spoils.

[lowtech] A rider brought {A_nameDef} a letter in a hand {A_pronoun} knew from the first line: {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} old captain, who now leads the fighters of {FACTION} against {ENEMY}. They're short of everything, {X_nameDef} writes, and {TALE} would make a difference.\n\nA share of the spoils will come back to the colony, if they win.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef}'s old commander, {X_nameDef}, has sent a message over the comms. {X_nameDef} now leads {FACTION}'s militia against {ENEMY}, and the campaign is short of supplies: {TALE} would keep them going.\n\nA share of whatever they take will come back to the colony, if they win.

li.label: Send {TALE} (they may lose)
li.outcome: The supplies go out with {FACTION}'s rider, along with a note from {A_nameDef} to {A_possessive} old commander.

li.label: Send good wishes only
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} writes back with good wishes and no supplies, and doesn't say much at supper.

coming.li: Word from {TALE}'s campaign against {ENEMY} is due in about {DAYS}.

done.li: [won,lowtech] {TALE} has written from the field: {FACTION} broke {ENEMY}'s line, and the supplies from the colony helped do it. A wagon came with the letter, loaded with the colony's share of the spoils: {ITEM}.
[won,!lowtech] A message from {TALE}: {FACTION}'s militia drove {ENEMY} back, and the colony's supplies kept them going when it counted. The colony's share of the spoils came with it: {ITEM}.

[lost] {TALE} has written from the field, briefly. The campaign against {ENEMY} went badly, and {FACTION} have fallen back to their own lands. The colony's supplies were well used, {TALE} writes, and won't be forgotten.

cancelled.li: No word has come back from {TALE}'s campaign, and with things as they are between the colony and {FACTION}, none will.

texts.li: [healer] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} walked a long way to find {A_nameDef}. Years ago, when {A_nameDef} was still a healer by trade, {A_pronoun} set {X_nameDef}'s broken leg and sat up three nights with the fever after. {X_nameDef} never forgot it, and has come with a gift.

[doctor] A traveler of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, asked at the gate for {A_nameDef} by name. {A_nameDef} pulled {X_nameDef} through a bad fever on the road, years ago, and had nearly forgotten. {X_nameDef} hadn't, and has come with a gift.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to see {A_nameDef}, who once saved {X_possessive} life with a needle, a lamp and a long night. {X_nameDef} has brought a gift, and says the debt is bigger than any gift.

li.label: Accept the gift
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sets the gift out on {A_nameDef}'s table piece by piece, and won't hear a word against it.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay on (may say no)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} says yes before the question is finished, and asks {A_nameDef} where {X_pronoun} can sleep.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} would like nothing better, but there's family waiting at home. The gift stays, though, and so does the thanks.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to spread the word
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} promises to tell every settlement on the road home about the colony's healer. The neighbors will hear of {A_nameDef}.

texts.li: [outlaw] Mending the lining of an old coat, {A_nameDef} found a map folded into the seam. {A_nameDef} drew it years ago, as {TALE}, to mark where a share of the takings was buried, and had forgotten it was there.\n\nThe place is a few days' travel from the colony. Whatever was hidden there may still be there.

[soldier] In the bottom of an old kitbag, {A_nameDef} found a map from the war, with a supply cache marked on it in a hand {A_pronoun} doesn't recognize. The unit that buried it never came back for it, as far as {A_nameDef} knows.\n\nIt's a few days' travel from here.

[trader] {A_nameDef} found an old ledger at the bottom of a chest, and pressed between its pages a map from {A_possessive} trading days, with a stash of goods marked on it. It's a few days' travel, and {A_nameDef} never told anyone else where it was.

[noble] Among the few things {A_nameDef} brought from {A_possessive} family's house is a book of old estate maps. Tucked in the back is one {A_nameDef} had never noticed: an old lodge a few days' travel from the colony, with something marked beneath its cellar.

[scholar] Sorting through old notes, {A_nameDef} found a map copied from an archive years ago, of a ruin {A_pronoun} always meant to visit. It's a few days' travel from the colony, and the archive's notes say something was left there.

{A_nameDef} found an old map among {A_possessive} things, from before {A_pronoun} came here. A spot is marked on it, a few days' travel from the colony. {A_nameDef} can't remember who drew it, but it still looks like it means something.

li.label: Follow it up
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} copies the old marks onto the colony's own map. Whoever goes will need to travel.

li.label: Keep it as a keepsake
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} folds the map back up and puts it away with {A_possessive} things.

outcomes.li: [gone] {A_nameDef} compares the old map with the colony's own and can't make them agree. Whatever it marked isn't there any more.

texts.li: [fossil] {A_nameDef} came running in with a split stone held in both hands. Pressed into the inside is the shape of a shell, perfectly clear, from some sea that dried up long before anyone lived here.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to know everything about it. {B_nameDef} knows more than most, if {B_pronoun} can spare the time.

[coin] {A_nameDef} dug an old coin out of the mud by the path, green with age, stamped with a face that none of the adults recognize.\n\n{A_nameDef} has polished it on {A_possessive} sleeve until it shines, and wants to know whose face it is. {B_nameDef} might be able to guess.

[skull] {A_nameDef} brought home a bird's skull from the woods, white and light as paper, and set it beside {A_possessive} plate at supper. {A_nameDef} wants to know what kind of bird it was and how it flew.\n\n{B_nameDef} has offered to look at it with {A_objective}.

[geode] {A_nameDef} cracked open a round gray stone by the stream and found it full of purple crystal inside. {A_nameDef} has shown it to every person in the colony at least twice.\n\n{B_nameDef} could explain how the crystals got in there.

[machine] {A_nameDef} pulled something out of an old junk pile: a scorched circuit board with a tiny screen that still glows faintly when it's tilted. {A_nameDef} is sure it's important.\n\n{B_nameDef} could take it apart with {A_objective} and explain what it was.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} study it with {A_objective}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} spend the evening bent over it, and {A_nameDef} goes to bed with a head full of questions and a page of drawings.

li.label: Let {A_objective} keep it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} puts it on the shelf over {A_possessive} bed, and checks on it every morning.

li.label: Trade it ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The find goes to the next trader for {COUNT} silver. {A_nameDef} watches it go.

texts.li: [game] {PET_nameDef} trotted in from the fields with {BEAST} in {PET_possessive} jaws and laid it at {A_nameDef}'s feet. {A_nameDef} has been praising {PET_objective} all morning, and there's fresh meat for the pot.

[herbs] {PET_nameDef} came back from the woods with a muddy mouthful of healing herbs, roots and all, and dropped them in {A_nameDef}'s lap. {A_nameDef} is telling anyone who'll listen that {PET_nameDef} knew exactly what {PET_pronoun} was doing.

[purse] {PET_nameDef} came home with a small leather purse, chewed at one corner, and wouldn't give it up until {A_nameDef} traded a bone for it. Inside: {COUNT} silver. Some traveler on the road will be patting their pockets tonight.
[component] {PET_nameDef} dug something out of the scrap heap and carried it proudly to {A_nameDef}: a component, slightly chewed and still in working order.
[nothing] {PET_nameDef} came back from the fields carrying an old boot that doesn't belong to anyone in the colony, and laid it at {A_nameDef}'s feet like a trophy. {A_nameDef} has put it on a shelf.

[lowtech,other] {A_nameDef} struck wood while digging and uncovered an old chest bound in iron, its lock rusted solid. It's heavy, and something inside shifts when it's tilted.\n\n{B_nameDef} thinks the lock can be worked open without damage, given time. It could also be broken open, or sold sealed to a rider of {FACTION} for {COUNT} silver.

[!lowtech,other] {A_nameDef} turned up a sealed supply crate, buried long ago, with a dead keypad and its seals intact. Whatever is inside has been dry all this time.\n\n{B_nameDef} could try to open it properly. It could also be pried open, or sold to {FACTION} for {COUNT} silver, unopened.

[mining,other] Cutting into the hillside, {A_nameDef} broke into a small hollow with a crate in it, sealed and stacked as neatly as the day someone left it there.\n\n{B_nameDef} thinks the lock can be opened without breaking anything. It could also be broken open, or sold sealed to {FACTION} for {COUNT} silver.

[same] Digging outside, {A_nameDef} found an old sealed crate with a stubborn lock. {A_nameDef} has the best hands in the colony, and thinks the lock could be worked open without breaking anything.\n\nIt could also be broken open, or sold sealed to {FACTION} for {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} work the lock open
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spends the afternoon on the lock.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} spends the afternoon on the lock.

li.label: Break it open (it may break what's inside)
Sell it sealed ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: A rider of {FACTION} pays {COUNT} silver for the crate and hauls it away, still sealed. The colony will never know what was in it.

outcomes.li: [careful,safe] {B_nameDef} spends the afternoon on the lock and opens it without a scratch. Everything inside is dry and whole: {ITEM}.
[careful,risk] {B_nameDef} gets the lock open cleanly, but the seal had failed years ago and most of what was inside has rotted. What's left: {ITEM}.
[broken,safe] A few good swings and the lid comes off. Inside: {ITEM}.
[broken,risk] The lid gives on the third blow, and so does a good deal of what was under it. What survived: {ITEM}.
